plan.title: Lab 11 starting-state check does not verify its required tools

narratives.Description: Lab 11 lists Node.js, npm, Git, Task, and uv as required tools but enters fixture creation without proving that each command resolves, so an absent tool can leave disposable state before the learner sees the setup failure. This story adds the established Labs 7 and 10 fail-closed version prefix and focused regression coverage while preserving the printed-path handoff, candidate-platform statement, and absence of Task or uv version pins.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Update `labs/11-testing-gates-and-evidence.md` so its Environment and starting-state shell fence enables fail-closed behavior and runs all five version commands before `create`, while leaving the `LAB11_ROOT` copy step after the visible create output.
2. Extend `scripts/verify-module-11.mjs` to require the ordered fail-closed prefix and preserve the candidate-platform and no-pin boundaries.
3. Add positive and negative fixtures in `scripts/verify-module-11.test.mjs` that prove a missing command, missing fail-closed option, or reordered `create` is rejected by the focused check.
narratives.UserStory: As a Lab 11 learner, I want required tools checked before fixture creation, so that I can classify setup failures without mutating an attempt.
narratives.Traces: Accepted bound remedy on https://github.com/deftai/directive-training/issues/59#issuecomment-5786102328, independently audited in comment 5787643424 and confirmed by synthesis comment 5787725610; relieves recorded pain P1.
narratives.Overview:
## Learner context

Independent Windows/PowerShell pilot of the required 0.119.5 course path, following the course in order as a mid/senior engineer.

## Problem

`labs/11-testing-gates-and-evidence.md` lists Node.js 20+, npm, Git, Task, and uv under **Environment and starting-state check**, but the first executable block immediately runs the fixture's `create` verb. It provides no literal `node --version`, `npm --version`, `git --version`, `task --version`, or `uv --version` checks and no pass criteria for those tools.

The other executable labs teach that a starting-state check is a gate. Here a learner can mutate a disposable attempt before discovering that Task or uv is missing or incompatible.

## Pain experienced

The mandatory course-wide pre-check had to be reconstructed by searching several later lab pages. Lab 11 cannot independently prove its own stated environment, which makes a failure after `create` harder to classify as tooling versus exercise behavior.

## Proposed fix

Add a platform-neutral version block before `create`, plus PowerShell syntax where needed, and state the acceptance criteria. At minimum check Node, npm, Git, Task, and uv; either require the verified Task/uv versions or explicitly state the supported variance.

## Reproduction

1. Open `labs/11-testing-gates-and-evidence.md`.
2. Read **Environment and starting-state check**.
3. Observe the required-tool list followed directly by `node .../gates-lab.mjs create`.

No Directive source or framework internals were consulted.

## 1. Bind Labs 7 and 10's version prefix
class: sharpens-framing

Evidence. At dispatch SHA `a484f30613f16d1da3c8f7a01edb5d67e562a12e`, `labs/11-testing-gates-and-evidence.md:28-40` lists Node.js 20+, npm, Git, Task, and uv, then the first fence is `node labs/fixtures/11-testing-gates-and-evidence/gates-lab.mjs create` with no `--version` lines. `labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:54-64` and `labs/10-implementation-golden-path.md:44-54` run `set -eu`, then `node` / `npm` / `git` / `task` / `uv --version`, then `create` in one fence. Those Environment sections contain no `3.50.0` or `0.11.10`. Capstone starting-state is the page that names those versions. `node scripts/verify-module-11.mjs` exits 0 and does not lock version-command presence. Lab 11's lab record names no Task or uv version.

Failure mode. Following the issue body's "require the verified Task/uv versions or state the supported variance" adds a Lab 11-only pin or an unmeasured variance table. Labs 7 and 10 already treat presence as the gate: the commands must run, and a missing executable stops the fence. Lab 7's later `201` note is expected-failures attribution, not a starting-state pin.

Disposition. Insert the five `--version` commands so a missing tool stops before `create`. Keep Lab 11's printed-path `LAB11_ROOT` copy step. Exact Task/uv pins and a variance table stay out of this recut.

## 2. Fail-closed is the shell option with those lines
class: sharpens-framing

Evidence. Lab 11's first fence (`:38-40`) has no `set -eu`. A `/tmp` probe of `missingcmd --version` then `echo REACHED_NEXT_LINE` printed `REACHED_NEXT_LINE` under bash and zsh without `-e` (exit 0) and stopped under `bash -e` / `zsh -e` (exit 127). Labs 7 and 10 keep the version lines inside `set -eu` before `create`.

Failure mode. Five `--version` lines pasted into Lab 11's current fence still reach `create` when `task` or `uv` is absent. The named pain stays open.

Disposition. Place the version commands in a fail-closed fence with `create`, matching Labs 7 and 10. Keep Lab 11's two-step printed-path export.

## 3. The Windows condensed route is a second surface
class: sharpens-framing

Evidence. Labs 7 and 10 open Environment with a dedicated zsh terminal; that section has no PowerShell fence. Each lab's Native Windows PowerShell 7.4+ route starts at `create` with no `--version` prefix and already sets `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` (Lab 7 after `:412`, Lab 10 after `:277`, Lab 11 after `:270`; Lab 11 first `create` at `:282`). `verify-module-11.mjs` requires the lab prose to keep Windows as a candidate.

Failure mode. A new Environment PowerShell starting-state on Lab 11 only is a platform-claim change, outside the Labs 7/10 identity. Patching only the sh fence leaves the Windows condensed route as Labs 7 and 10 already leave it.

Disposition. Bind the Environment sh fence to Labs 7 and 10. Same-page `--version` lines on Lab 11's existing Native Windows route are optional consistency under the existing Stop preference. Keep the candidate-platform sentence.

## 4. Tool resolution already lives on install
class: footnote

`createAttempt()` in `labs/fixtures/11-testing-gates-and-evidence/gates-lab.mjs` writes the OS-temp fixture and runs `git`; it does not call `findExecutable` or `createIsolatedTools`. Those run in `installAttempt`. A missing `task` or `uv` already fails there with `Required executable not found`. Page-level versions matching Labs 7 and 10 are the existing mechanism for stopping before that leftover attempt.

## 5. Neighbor surfaces stay on their pages
class: footnote

`createIsolatedTools` also requires Python; Labs 7 and 10 omit `python --version`. Course-map prerequisites and Lab 2's Confirm-the-tools Pass are other pages. Lab 11's expected-failures table, like Labs 7 and 10, has no missing-tool row.

## Road not taken

Page-level versions (Labs 7 and 10) versus adding `findExecutable` to `createAttempt`. Install already names a missing executable. The helper-side check would fire even if a learner skipped the page block. Flip if Labs 7 and 10 resolved tools inside `create`; they do not.

Steelmanning an exact Task/uv pin: capstone already confirms `3.50.0` / `0.11.10`, and Lab 7 attributes a `201` wrapper to that Task version. Flip if Lab 11's aggregate evidence depended on that wrapper exit. The helper invokes `task --silent` and retains JSON; it does not teach the `201` contract in starting-state.
